page_partition_scope: Every page of the sixteen individual canonical PDFs per application appears exactly once; the three duplicate bundles remain only in canonical directories.
selection_scope: Explicit editorial selection by scientific role; all source pages retained, no benchmark or episode selection.

results/main/beamforming/task_performanc.selection_rationale: Shows moderate-dimensional task losses and paired same-episode controls.
results/main/beamforming/task_performanc.proposed_latex_caption: Held-out disturbance power relative to the known-covariance oracle at $n=32,64,128$ and $L/n=1$, together with paired moving-task episode differences. Snapshot losses are averaged within each independent episode. The mean curve has pointwise 95\% confidence bands; paired boxes describe episode differences, not confidence intervals. Complete training-count, control and motion-condition grids remain supplementary.
results/main/beamforming/task_performanc.full_source_caption: Task losses on common independent test episodes. Held-out disturbance or query losses are averaged within each episode before computing pointwise Student 95\% intervals. Only the posterior-mean curve carries a confidence band in the main absolute-loss panels. The contact paired panel isolates the same-data modal, matched-isotropic and regularized spectral controls; response-only GREAT remains in its absolute-loss panel and the full supplementary grid. Contact paired points show mean loss differences and pointwise Student 95\% confidence intervals across independent episodes, including every episode outlier; they are not posterior intervals. Beamforming paired boxes show the distribution of episode differences, not confidence intervals. The same-$A_t$ modal and matched-isotropic controls isolate posterior moments; GREAT and application-specific controls have separately validated settings and their stated information. Beamforming power ratios are $10\log_{10}(P/P_{\mathrm{oracle}})$, where the denominator is true-covariance oracle output power. Oracle quantities are evaluation-only. This cohort has 256 independent test episodes per condition; snapshots and queries are averaged within each episode.

results/main/beamforming/noise_adaptatio.selection_rationale: Shows the declared noise-change intervention and causal variance learning.
results/main/beamforming/noise_adaptatio.proposed_latex_caption: Causal variance learning under the predeclared noise-change intervention. Fits use completed, nonoverlapping past blocks and affect future variances only; every observation is assimilated once. Variance bands describe interquartile repeated-episode spread, not a posterior over the variance. Future-task and excluded-observation score intervals are pointwise 95\% intervals across independent episodes. Empirical-Bayes plug-in scales omit scale uncertainty and are outside the fixed-variance theorem. Motion and signal-power interventions remain supplementary.
results/main/beamforming/noise_adaptatio.full_source_caption: Actual causal variance learning from completed nonoverlapping past blocks. Each observation is corrected once; a fit updates only subsequent variances while retaining the streamed subspace belief. Known coordinate changes are aligned before block fitting. Curves show saved trajectory/episode summaries; variance bands are interquartile repeated-episode spread, not a posterior over variance. Future-task and pre-observation score intervals are pointwise 95\% intervals across independent episodes. Each page retains one predeclared noise-, motion-, or signal-power intervention. The contact supplementary density pages show one predeclared episode: panels (a,b) of the first density page use $t=32,96$, and panel (a) of the following density page uses $t=192$; pre-correction $A_t^-$ is converted to the wrist-frame normal law $q_{-A_t^-}$ with normalizer $\psi_1(-A_t^-)=\psi_2(A_t^-)-\operatorname{tr}(A_t^-)$. The three orthographic spheres share a density scale; panel (b) of the following density page shows the physical-query risk at all three checkpoints, $v_t^T(M_t^--(M_t^-)^2)v_t$ at the recorded physical query. This is individual belief uncertainty, distinct from the repeated-episode variance bands and from calibration. Empirical-Bayes plug-in scales omit their uncertainty and are outside the fixed-true-variance theorem.

results/supplementary/beamforming/block_.proposed_latex_caption: Exact discounted aggregation, delayed actions and constant-subspace approximation are separate checks. Aggregation retains the boundary factor $\beta^L$, within-block weights, per-observation variances and recorded noncommuting transport. Numerical zeros are displayed at a $10^{-16}$ plotting floor; full tolerances remain in the tables. Delayed actions are evaluated only after a block arrives, with common endpoints and physical output age reported separately. results/supplementary/beamforming/predic.proposed_latex_caption: Actual-recursion calibration with distinct state, clean-response and noisy-next-observation targets. Pages separate joint prior-predictive sampling, fixed-state repetitions and drift diagnostics. Vertical intervals are pointwise exact binomial uncertainty across independent episodes, not credible uncertainty. All intervals are evaluated at their declared time before the scored future observation is seen. Appended pages show 95% report-size distributions at t=64 for every probability regime. State-ball sizes are chordal radii, obtained by taking the square root of each recorded squared-distance upper threshold; HPD energy thresholds are not used as geometric widths. Scalar sizes are upper minus lower in the n=3 fixture units. Boxes show the median and interquartile range across independent episodes, with 1.5-IQR whiskers and every outlier; this spread is not a posterior distribution or a confidence interval over width. Proper-score checks are separate. Validation-fitted widths do not establish a matched-coverage advantage if achieved test coverage misses its target. Numerical mass and quantile precision are separate from mean accuracy. Both applications use n=3 reliability fixtures. On the inclusion pages, panel (a) checks latent-subspace inclusion in its HPD set; panel (b) reports the clean scalar $q^H Pq$ for a known unit complex query $q$; panel (c) reports the noisy scalar $\operatorname{Re}(u_{t,1})$. Contact observations are real. On the appended size pages, panels (a), (b), (c) show the state-ball chordal radius, clean scalar width and noisy scalar width, respectively. These are 128 independent test episodes per fixed checkpoint and regime.

results/main/beamforming/computation_tim.selection_rationale: Shows the computational cost at explicitly declared action and learning cadences.
results/main/beamforming/computation_tim.proposed_latex_caption: Warmed single-thread costs at the stated action, uncertainty-reporting and variance-learning cadences. Full-cycle timings, nonoverlapping phase costs, and memory accounting have separate scopes. Action cadence differs from the fixed block of 32 observations per scale fit. Repeated clocks quantify host timing variation; they are not additional statistical episodes or worst-case deadlines.
results/main/beamforming/computation_tim.full_source_caption: Warmed single-thread pipeline cost at actual action, reporting and learning schedules. Action cadence is labelled in observations and is distinct from the fixed $L=32$ observations per EM fit. EM bars use two or four iterations, and optional uncertainty reports occur every 32 observations. Correction, modal/mean action, uncertainty report and variance fitting are nonoverlapping phases; a native moment routine already includes its eigensystem. Medians and upper quantiles use the declared randomized repetitions. Phase stacks sum per-phase medians and need not equal the median full-cycle wall time. Stored state and tracked allocation have separate scopes; native workspaces and RSS are not silently included. Timings are host measurements, not worst-case deadlines. Synthetic spectra and statistical-state task fixtures remain distinct. Task/cost trade-off points use the same predeclared episode 0, not the population task-loss mean; clock repetitions quantify execution variability only.
